Chapter 8: The Rival Is...

The moment he saw the mission on the panel, Jiang Nian was a bit dazed. Five thousand yuan?

That's right, this guy always looked at the reward first when it came to missions. What the mission actually was didn't matter.

Since he was on his way home and Xu Qianqian was talking to him, Jiang Nian only had time to glance at the reward before quickly closing the panel.

After getting the system, Jiang Nian's mindset had changed.

In twenty years, he would get a divorce.

If he continued on his original life path, he would have twenty terrible and painful years. Cowardice, low self-esteem, depravity, accomplishing nothing, a failed marriage.

If the future was destined to be a tragedy, then to hell with it.

Before they knew it, the two had arrived downstairs. Just as Jiang Nian was about to head up the dark stairwell, he was suddenly stopped by Xu Qianqian. He couldn't help but turn back to look at her.

"What's wrong?"

"The 'Returning Home' poem: 'I realize that the past cannot be remonstrated,' what comes after that?" she asked. In the darkness, only the girl's blurry silhouette could be seen, her voice clear and bright.

Jiang Nian paused for a moment. He had memorized all the ancient poems for the Gaokao Chinese exam during his memory period, so he recited it subconsciously.

"...'but I know that the future can still be pursued. I have not strayed too far down the wrong path; I feel that I am right today and that I was wrong yesterday.'"

Xu Qianqian took a step forward, and in the darkness, the outline of the girl's delicate face became a little clearer. Her eyes, a mixture of light and shadow, were like water as she spoke with a serious expression.

"It's not too late now. There's still time for everything."

He understood Xu Qianqian was talking about the Gaokao, but in that instant, Jiang Nian still couldn't help but feel a little dazed.

The missions in the system were all related to Xu Qianqian. If it wasn't too late at thirty-eight, what about now at eighteen? Was he on the wrong path from the very beginning?

The person most suited for him might be right by his side.

Just as this thought arose, he heard Xu Qianqian add a sentence.

"I have a set of English practice tests here..."

"Ahem, I get it." Jiang Nian acted fast, directly stopping Xu Qianqian's attempt to pull the tests out of her schoolbag at the drop of a hat. "It's getting late. Can we look at it tomorrow?"

Xu Qianqian rolled her eyes at him, then went upstairs with a flick of her elegant ponytail.

"Whatever you want."

Back at home.

Jiang Nian tossed his schoolbag aside and was about to take a shower, planning to lie in bed and take a closer look at the panel mission. But he was stopped by his mom, who asked about the express delivery.

"Oh, I bought shoes for you and Old Jiang. They were on sale, a pretty good deal."

"Why'd you waste money like that? You should have just bought them for yourself." His mom started to nag. "It's not like I don't have shoes to wear. Don't always spend money so frivolously."

Hearing this, Old Jiang also walked over and added a few words. It was nothing more than saying it was a good thing to be able to earn money, but he should keep it for himself, as he would need a lot of money in the future.

Jiang Nian covered his ears and rushed straight to the bathroom, impervious to their words, refusing to listen.

As it turned out, parents were creatures who would always say one thing and do another.

By the time Jiang Nian came out of the shower, Old Jiang's new leather shoes had already been polished and placed on the top shelf of the shoe rack. His mom's pair was no exception, with the shoelaces tied neatly.

Wiping his hair, he couldn't help but smile as he returned to his room.

Jiang Nian skillfully turned on the air conditioner and electric fan one by one, letting his hair dry naturally. With one hand, he picked up the water glass on his desk, and with the other, he opened the system's mission panel.

"Hmm? A love rival?"

He glanced at the mission description, pausing at the line "didn't speak a word from high school to university." What kind of a hardcore person was this? A secret crush storyline, was it?

Jiang Nian wasn't surprised at all that someone had a crush on Xu Qianqian. He had seen Xu Qianqian as a rival since childhood. They knew each other inside and out, and the filter of distance had long since vanished.

In the eyes of outsiders, Xu Qianqian was a well-behaved girl with fair skin, a good figure, and excellent grades.

In the Jiang family's master bedroom.

Li Hongmei tossed and turned, unable to sleep. Thinking about the shoes her son had bought for them, she couldn't resist nudging her husband in the dark.

Old Jiang instantly shivered, his body tensing up as he pretended to be asleep. "Stop pretending. You're awake," Li Hongmei said coldly.

"...Huh? Hongmei?" Old Jiang turned over, looking as if he had just woken up and could barely open his eyes. "It's so late, the neighbors are all asleep. What's gotten into you?"

With just one sentence, he had maxed out all his buffs.

Li Hongmei was speechless. "I'm talking to you about something serious. Don't you think we should intervene with Xiao Nian's gaming? Earning money is a good thing, but what if it affects his studies?"

"How about we talk to him tomorrow and tell him not to play anymore?"

Old Jiang thought for a moment and said, "I don't think that's appropriate."

"What's not appropriate about it? Do you know how important the third year of high school is?" Li Hongmei grew anxious, sitting up. "If he doesn't get into a good university, he'll hit a wall everywhere he goes when he enters the workforce."

"I know all that. Don't get anxious. Let me analyze it for you slowly." Old Jiang was a slow-tempered man, always patient. "The kid just earned some money. Who's the first person he thought of?"

"I estimate that Xiao Nian spent at least fifteen or sixteen hundred. He might have spent all the money he earned on us—on food we ate, on shoes we wear."

Hearing this, Li Hongmei's frown also relaxed.

"Xiao Nian is a good kid, but good kids can't find jobs. What's he going to do if he doesn't go to university?"

"Don't be anxious, let me finish." Old Jiang placed a hand on his wife's shoulder. "Let's wait until the school's monthly exam next week. After the results are out, we can talk to Xiao Nian then."

"And I'm telling you, you should praise the kid more these few days. Don't always wear such a long face."

"I know, I know, you're so talkative." Li Hongmei rolled herself up in the blanket. "Time to sleep, time to sleep. I still have to work tomorrow. All this chattering, makes you think you're so smart."

Old Jiang: "..."

The next day.

After going out to buy breakfast, Jiang Nian made a point to get a portion for Xu Qianqian, so the two of them "coincidentally" walked to school together again.

Xu Qianqian pouted. "To be overly attentive for no reason is to have bad intentions."

"How am I being overly attentive for no reason? Didn't you agree to teach me math?" Jiang Nian quickened his pace to catch up, and the two of them wound through the narrow alley to reach the main street outside.

"Oh." Xu Qianqian took a bite of her vegetable bun with a clear conscience, squinting as she sipped her soy milk. "Why do you always buy soy milk? I want to drink strawberry-flavored You Suan Ru."

"Stop fooling around. Soy milk is good for your brain," he said.

The sunlight on the street was clear, the green trees were lush, and dappled sunlight fell on the uneven road along the storefronts. The breakfast stalls were crowded with students, shrouded in white steam.

"Huh? I've never heard that soy milk can boost your brain?" Xu Qianqian, wearing white sneakers, walked ahead and turned her head to ask curiously, "Isn't it walnut milk that boosts your brain?"

Soy milk is rich in plant-based estrogen, which is food for the baby, so naturally, it also nourishes the baby's brain.

Jiang Nian thought to himself, *It's not your brain I'm trying to boost.* "Who told you that walnuts boost your brain? That's completely a psychological effect."

"Is that so?"

Sunlight fell through the strands of the girl's hair, and the sounds of their discussion faded into the distance.

As they were about to enter the school gate, Jiang Nian asked casually, as if it were nothing.

"Hey, is there a guy in your class named Zhou Haifei?"

Hearing this, Xu Qianqian stopped in her tracks.

"A guy?"

"Yeah, what's wrong?"

"There is someone named Zhou Haifei in our class, but..." Xu Qianqian looked at Jiang Nian, her pink lips slightly parted. "She's a girl. Her name should be Zhou Haifei (菲)."

Jiang Nian was stunned. "A girl?"

What the hell! Is this a lesbian thing?

(End of this chapter)
